proof.criterion: A7: a real listener, built from the tree and run against a real NATS server with the environment the hub renders, answers a /v1 request carrying the hub's own address and refuses one carrying another; with that environment as it is rendered today, it refuses the hub's own address.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary, built from packages/envoy/cmd/listener in this tree, running against a real nats-server container, started from the very core.ListenerConfig gcp:NatsHub renders for a hub whose tailnet name is set (ENVOY_ALLOWED_HOSTS=example-host-a.example-tailnet.ts.net, composed by core.TailnetHostName, never a literal). CI job envoy-infra-go, step 8 'Live tests of envoy-infra against nats-server (natslive)'; no Legion worker machine has a container runtime, so this proof runs in CI and nowhere else.
proof.command: GitHub Actions run 39840249110, job 120039730704 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/39840249110/job/120039730704), step 'Live tests of envoy-infra against nats-server (natslive)': go test -tags natslive ./core/ ./seed/ from packages/envoy/infra. Locally, on a machine with a container runtime: go test -tags natslive -run TestHubListenerServesItsTailnetName ./core/
proof.observed: The step's conclusion is success, so TestHubListenerServesItsTailnetName passed on both images (subtests /2.10 and /hub): the listener reached "status":"healthy", answered POST /v1/interests/subscribe carrying Host: example-host-a.example-tailnet.ts.net with exactly 200, and answered the same request carrying Host: other.example-tailnet.ts.net with exactly 421 and a body naming ENVOY_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Every other step of that job (gofmt, go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./..., go test ./...) is success at the same head.
proof.negativeControl: The second listener in the same test, on a NATS server of its own, started with that same configuration minus AllowedHosts — the environment the plugin rendered before this change — answered the hub's own address example-host-a.example-tailnet.ts.net with 421 and a body naming ENVOY_ALLOWED_HOSTS (the bug this issue is about, reproduced beside the fix), while still answering Host: 127.0.0.1:<port> with 200, so the refusal is the host guard (cmd/listener/apiauth.go, servesHost) and not a listener that failed to come up.

trickyParts: Checks run in this pod at the head, all green: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"; go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./...; go test ./... (packages/envoy/infra); go test -tags natslive -run '^$' ./core/ ./seed/ (compiles and links the tagged package, which is as far as a pod goes); bash .github/scripts/check-private-names.sh from the repository root.

gcp/data_disk_test.go's two tests (TestTheDataDiskIsFormattedOnlyWhenItReadsAsZerosToItsEnd, TestARefusedDataDiskIsNeverFormattedOnALaterBoot) fail in this pod and fail for anyone without e2fsprogs: the pod has no mkfs.ext4, blkid or blockdev, and those tests fail rather than skip by design (packages/envoy/infra/AGENTS.md, 'Tests'). They touch nothing this change touches and are success in CI at this head (envoy-infra-go's 'Unit test envoy-infra' step). Every pod run above was therefore -skip'd on those two names alone.

The allowed-host rule is mirrored in core rather than imported: a non-test import of packages/envoy/internal/config would add that package to go list -deps ./cmd/..., which is the plugin's release-cut path list, so every change to the listener's own configuration would cut a plugin release. core/allowed_hosts_agreement_test.go drives both rules over one table and asserts the import is absent, so the mirror cannot drift silently or be replaced by a production import.

An entry is rendered as the operator wrote it: not normalised, not de-duplicated. The listener normalises at boot (config.HostName) and compares with slices.Contains, so a duplicate costs nothing and a normalised-away difference still matches, while normalising in the plugin would show a value in pulumi preview nobody typed.

ce-simplify-code ran once at 73555fed0265 and applied one finding two reviewers raised independently: the hub prepends its own address before core's per-entry check, so an operator's first listener.allowedHosts entry was refused as allowedHosts[1] under core's input name, which contradicted this change's own documentation. core.CheckAllowedHosts(input, hosts) now owns the rule and each caller names its own path; the gcp rows pin listener.allowedHosts[0] and [1] for the operator's own first and second entries. Three findings were skipped: two test-literal dedups (one would give the existing postListener a 10 s timeout it never had), and routing gcp/dispatch.go's three hand-written MagicDNS joins through core.TailnetHostName, which is outside this diff and is the pull request's one Fast-follow line.
deviations: The plan's T6.3 spells the live listener's config without ListenHost; it is started with ListenHost: "127.0.0.1" so the environment is byte-for-byte the one resolveListener renders for a hub. The guard reads the Host header alone, so the proof is unaffected and strictly closer to the hub.

The plan's T4.5 and T2 put the allowed-host refusal rows under core's 'allowedHosts' path everywhere. The applied simplify finding changed the hub's half: a gcp refusal names listener.allowedHosts and the operator's own index. core's own rows are unchanged, and packages/envoy/infra/docs/nats-hub.md quotes the refusal as the code now emits it.
discoveredComplexity: Merging cuts an envoy-infra release (.github/workflows/release-envoy-infra.yaml fires on every push to main under packages/envoy/**). The fix reaches the hub only when dispatch://INFRA-120 pins that version, sets tailnetDnsName and moves listenerImage; nothing in the deployment repository changes here. The production check after the close will name the tag the merge produced and the merge commit to the session that owns INFRA-120, so it can verify the tag carries the merge before it moves the pin.

A client that dials the hub by its bare MagicDNS label or its tailnet IP is still refused unless that address is in listener.allowedHosts: only the fully-qualified name is rendered. The architect settled this (the deployment hands its clients http://<hostname>.<tailnetDnsName>:9020, so they are served as they stand), and the operator document says to check what a hub's clients actually dial before the image moves.

envoy-infra-go is not a required check on main (main's ruleset requires lint, typecheck, test and pr-title only), so nothing in the workflow sends this change back if the natslive proof goes red. The run is named by id in the pull request body for the tester and the merger to read by name.
